bug_semantics: SWE-agent's trajectory inspector HTTP server (sweagent inspector) handles GET /trajectory/<path> in Handler.do_GET before delegating to SimpleHTTPRequestHandler, so the stdlib '..' sanitization never runs. serve_file_content then opens Path(self.traj_dir) / file_path with no resolve/is_relative_to containment check and load_content json.loads the target. Combined with TCPServer(('', port)) (0.0.0.0), Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, and no auth, an unauthenticated network client (or a cross-origin page via CORS) can send literal '..' segments (curl --path-as-is) and read trajectory-shaped JSON outside the served directory. Non-trajectory files typically 500; disclosure is constrained to JSON with history/trajectory/info, which can still carry repo contents, command output, and API keys.
flaw_origin: The unsanitized join, custom /trajectory/ route, all-interfaces bind, wildcard CORS, and json.load sink were first written together in the repository root commit that added inspector/server.py. Later history only reformats quotes, relocates the file into sweagent/inspector/, and extends inspector UI/stats; git log -L and -S show the Path(self.traj_dir)/file_path join was never rewritten.

reasoning: Vulnerability-first: GHSA-hpx7-jm9p-88gh / CVE-2026-75482 are live published records of a CWE-22 read in the inspector /trajectory/ handler. The mechanism is present on current main and on tagged v1.1.0 exactly as the issue describes (custom route bypasses SimpleHTTPRequestHandler sanitization; pathlib join does not reject '..'; json.load constrains the sink to trajectory-shaped JSON). Maintainer skepticism on PR #1414 does not withdraw or reject the advisory, so this is not FALSE_POSITIVE. BIC search used -L/-S/blame as leads, not AI-first inversion: the Path(self.traj_dir)/file_path join and /trajectory/ handler appear in root commit 5b143857cb7af8b22fd421a103429f76f5259f08 and nowhere earlier; the later package move is not a BIC. That commit has no parent, so parent absence of the vulnerable lines is vacuously verified and no squash members are reconstructable in public git. Commit-object authorship is human (Carlos E. Jimenez) with no AI trailers, hence NOT_AI. No fix SHA exists on origin/main; the case closes as unpatched with the concrete resolve-and-contain plus loopback/CORS remediation proposed in still-open PR #1505.

CVE-2026-75482/GHSA-hpx7-jm9p-88gh remain published; SWE-agent/SWE-agent#1472 is still open; candidate fixes #1414 and #1473 were closed unmerged and #1505 is open unmerged. potential_fix.approach: Resolve the /trajectory/ request against traj_dir (percent-decode, strip query/fragment, Path.resolve) and reject any result that is not inside the served directory; bind TCPServer to 127.0.0.1 by default with an explicit --host opt-in; drop Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *.
potential_fix.rationale: Containment on the joined path closes the CWE-22 read that bypasses SimpleHTTPRequestHandler; loopback default and removing wildcard CORS close the unauthenticated network and cross-origin vectors the advisory names. This matches the still-unmerged #1505/#1472 remediation.
